On the small étale site of a scheme $X$, a *torsion abelian sheaf* is a sheaf whose **geometric stalks** are torsion abelian groups; a derived complex $K\in D^+(X_{\acute et})$ has torsion cohomology when all its **cohomology sheaves** $H^i(K)$ are torsion. The right derived functors $R\Gamma(X,-)$ and $Rf_*$ of étale global sections/direct image are defined for abelian sheaves or their complexes. A quasi-compact and quasi-separated (qcqs) scheme or morphism is explicitly required to assert preservation of torsion by higher cohomology or higher direct image.
